title: feature ideas: routing + caching scratchpad
summary: Rough PRD + notes for combining smart routing policies with prefix/KV caching to reduce cost and improve p99 latency for hosted API customers.
content:
Goal: explore a joined feature set where routing policies (by latency/cost/region) and prefix/KV caching work together to improve p99 latency and reduce token costs for common queries. Scratchpad + initial PRD outline.

Problem statement:
- Customers often have a small hot set of prompts (e.g., search summaries, assist prompts, product questions) that account for a large fraction of tokens.
- Current routing can send requests to cheaper compatible model variants but doesn't consider cached prefixes across variants.
- Missed opportunity: if we can reuse KV cache or prefix responses across model variants and route to nodes that have warm caches, we can reduce token generation and lower latency.

Hypothesis:
- Routing requests to instances with warm KV/prefix caches for similar prompts will lower p99 latency by ~20-40% for those workloads and reduce token costs by 10-25% for customers with a hot prompt distribution.

User segments & personas:
- Small-medium startups with predictable bot prompts (high repetition) and cost sensitivity.
- Customer support platforms with templated prompts.
- Platform teams wanting deterministic SLAs during peak bursts.

Key goals (success metrics):
- p99 latency reduction for targeted routes: target 20% improvement baseline.
- Token reduction: reduce generated tokens for cached flows by 10-25%.
- No regression on throughput or reliability (SLO 99.9% same).
- Observability: per-route cache hit rate surfaced in Console.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting core model weights or model-level cache sharing across incompatible architectures.
- Large changes to customer API surface in first iteration (aim to be transparent to API callers).

Approach / high-level design notes:
- Add routing policy type: cache-aware-routing. Policy can prefer instances with warm prefix/KV caches for a given route/key. Policy config options: prefer_by_hit_rate | prefer_by_latency | prefer_by_cost.
- Cache metadata: maintain lightweight bloom-filter-like prefix signatures per instance (small, periodically updated) to indicate presence of common prefixes without exposing user data.
- When routing, prefer instances with matching prefix signatures and compatible model variant. If none available, fallback to standard routing.
- Cross-variant cache reuse: allow reuse only when model variants are deemed KV-compatible (e.g., same architecture + compatible tokenizer + compatible quantization). Maintain compatibility table.
- Serve-time decisions should be cheap: routing decision must add <1ms overhead in the path. Use cached routing table per edge.

User stories / acceptance criteria:
- As an app engineer, I want frequent assistant prompts to hit warm caches so my latency drops and token usage decreases. Acceptance: for routes with cache-aware-routing enabled, cache-hit metric appears in Console and p99 latency improves for test prompt set.
- As a platform admin, I want to configure prefer_by_cost vs prefer_by_latency per route. Acceptance: setting toggles in route config and rollout to 10% of traffic behaves as expected.
- As an infra engineer, I want routing to fall back gracefully. Acceptance: if preferred instance is overloaded or cache inconsistent, request falls back within 50ms and error rate does not increase.

Telemetry & observability:
- New metrics: route.cache_hit_rate, instance.prefix_signature_age, route.cache_routing_decisions_count, cache_routing_fallback_count.
- Console: per-route breakdown with hit rate, saved_tokens_estimate, p50/p95/p99 latency delta vs baseline.

Privacy & security considerations:
- Prefix signatures must be privacy-preserving. Proposal: hashed prefix fingerprints salted per-customer and rotated. No raw prompt data leaves instance.
- For enterprise-private deployments, allow opt-out of sharing prefix-signature metadata with control plane; fall back to local-only routing.

Rollout plan / experiment ideas:
- Internal canary: enable on int cluster for synthetic traffic with known hot set. Validate hit rate and latency.
- Customer pilot: 3 customers (one SMB, one mid-market, one platform) opt-in for route-level beta. Monitor metrics for 4 weeks.
- Gradual percentage rollout with A/B: compare prefer_by_latency vs prefer_by_cost.

Risks / open questions (TODO):
- How often to refresh instance prefix signatures without adding too much network noise? (opt: 1-5 min?)
- Are bloom-filter false positives tolerable? Need cost/benefit analysis.
- Cross-variant cache correctness: how to guarantee KV-cache state matches (esp. caches derived from sampling)?
- Edge-case: long-running conversations with KV growth\u2014eviction policies and how they affect hit rate.
- Billing: how to attribute saved tokens vs routing cost (if cheaper model used but additional network hop required).

Implementation notes / rough tasks:
- Infra: add lightweight prefix signature generator + uploader, define format + TTL. (Raja)
- Serving runtime: add routing hook that consults cached instance metadata & compatibility table. (serving-runtime eng)
- Console: add metrics and route config UI. (Console team, Zoe)
- Product: define route config UX and defaults, experiment plan, customer comms. (me-Aisha)
- Security: review prefix signature privacy model; KMS considerations for enterprise.

Acceptance test plan:
- Synthetic load test with 1K common prompts; measure baseline vs cache-aware routing p99.
- Chaos test: kill preferred instance and ensure fallback within 50ms with no request loss.
- Privacy audit: ensure no raw prompts in metadata pipeline.

Next steps (this week):
- Sync with Raja + serving-runtime on feasibility of per-instance prefix signature (meeting Wed).
- Draft Confluence spec for cache metadata format (owners: Raja + me).
- Create Jira epic RDC-2543 with subtasks for infra/serving/console.

Notes / fragments (brainstorming):
- Could combine with prefetch idea: when a route hints a likely next prompt, prefetch KV into warm instances in the background. Need careful throttling.
- Could offer "cache-aware routing as a service" for Dedicated customers with SLA promise.
- Consider an offline profiler that mines customer traffic to propose route-level cacheable prompt sets.

References / related docs:
- linked: users/llm-prefetch-kv-cache-scratchpad.json (internal scratch)
- linked: shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/prefix-kv-design-notes (draft)

Open questions to bring to sync:
1) Max size of prefix signature per instance we can tolerate?
2) Compatibility rules for cross-variant reuse (who decides?)
3) What's reasonable TTL for signatures and frequency of refresh?
notes_short: Scratchpad for routing+cache feature. Next: sync w/ Raja Wed, draft Confluence, create Jira epic.
